title: bug: moe-agent.sh's daemon pre-flight deletes a Docker-run daemon's .moe/daemon.json, because `kill -0 <container pid>` fails on the host (moe-agent.sh:1924-1928), and then starts a second daemon on the same .moe/; only a Windows drive-letter projectPath gets the /health liveness probe (launcher twin of task-da89f620)
description:
Filed by hunt #23 (task-da51c48b), from the same real-docker run at moe/work-2026-10-24 2037e856 as task-da89f620. Read that row's EVIDENCE first.
- The container daemon writes {"port":19877,"pid":15,...} into the mounted project's .moe/daemon.json, and /health answers healthy for the project.
- On the host, `kill -0 15` reports "/bin/bash: line 1: kill: (15) - No such process" (exit 1).

PROBLEM (scripts/moe-agent.sh at 2037e856)
- :1873-1879: FOREIGN_DAEMON is set only when projectPath has the drive-letter form ("daemon.json written by a Windows-side daemon ... its PID is invisible here, so kill -0 would misread a live daemon as stale, delete its discovery file, and spawn a duplicate daemon onto the same .moe/").
- :1922-1928: a container record has a native path, so it falls through to `elif ! kill -0 "$PID"`. That prints "Stale daemon.json detected (PID 15 is not running)", runs `rm -f "$DAEMON_INFO"` and then autostarts a daemon. That is the duplicate the comment above warns about, and task-da89f620 demonstrates the two-writer result for the CLI.
- bash's `kill -0` also fails on EPERM (a root-owned host pid). So even a pid that is alive on the host reads as stale.
- moe-agent.ps1 (:986-1004) deletes nothing itself. On a dead pid it runs the daemon's own `start`, so task-da89f620 covers the ps1 path.

FIX DIRECTION
- Extend the FOREIGN_DAEMON test so a record carrying the pidNamespace from task-da89f620 that differs from `readlink /proc/self/ns/pid` also counts as foreign. A record whose value cannot be compared counts too.
- The existing probe_daemon_health loop then decides, and the record is never removed while /health answers for this project.
- A record without the field keeps today's kill -0 path.
- Prefer no new parity-checked strings. If moe-agent.ps1 does need a parity line, keep the change to that line.

PLACEMENT
- dependsOn task-da89f620, which fixes the field.
- dependsOn task-cd3887fe, which holds scripts/moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1.
- dependsOn task-bbd7ad2d and task-1dfec7a4, which hold moe-agent.ps1. Drop those two with moe.set_task_dependencies if the approved plan leaves moe-agent.ps1 untouched.
- Edit the wrapper with a TOOL-witnessed editor (project customRules).
- The natural test home is scripts/tests/daemon-json-cap.test.mjs, which already drives this pre-flight's daemon.json handling.
definitionOfDone: A scripts/tests case runs moe-agent.sh's daemon pre-flight against a daemon.json that carries a foreign pidNamespace and a dead pid, with a /health stub answering for the project. The case proves that the pre-flight reports the daemon reachable, keeps daemon.json and starts no daemon. The case fails against 2037e856's moe-agent.sh.
A record without pidNamespace, or with the host's own namespace, and a dead pid is still cleaned up as stale, as today; the existing daemon-json-cap cases pass unchanged.
bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh passes, and `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh` is clean.
